title: CR-015 Cut-Space Portrait
description: Source-conditioned art-style transformation: translate the verified CR-001 adult fashion photograph into a contemporary layered-paper pop-up diorama with discrete supportable cut components, layer spacing, and construction-generated shadows. Uses art_style_transform + paper_cut_layered + popup_diorama + newly_created. No TransformationPack (paper ArtMethod has no concept_refs; fragments emit on the non-lexical compiler path). Empty EraPack list—no historical craft authenticity claim and no named tradition attribution. Symbolic reference roles only; binary reference packaging is out of PromptRecipe scope. Operator must supply the verified CR-001 PNG (SHA-256 0dcf8af6cac15441d5e728f98ac53314442984d3a27a5dd193effa2bac46f41e) as the image input at generation time. See docs/CR_015_CUT_SPACE_PORTRAIT.md. No gallery image attached.

semantic_spec.request: Transform the referenced adult fashion photograph into a newly created contemporary layered-paper pop-up diorama construction. Preserve recognizable visual identity of the source adult figure, the distinguishing standing stance and key anatomical proportions, the overall evening-gown silhouette including the draped neckline and major gathered-fabric architecture, and the hairstyle silhouette, while explicitly authorizing selective omission of nonessential fine garment seams, repetitive tiny folds, satin microtexture and gloss, photographic skin shading, photographic highlight gradients, individual hair strands, and tiny detached features—translate those details into physically supported paper shapes or purposeful cut-out omissions rather than tracing them. Build the figure from discrete cut-paper components with crisp cut silhouettes, consistent paper thickness, matte fibrous stocks, and subtle cut-edge fibers; every apparently separate component must remain mechanically intelligible through a paper bridge, tab, folded support, hinge, glued or pasted overlap, or attachment to another supported layer—forbid unsupported floating paper islands. Express foreground paper elements, middle-layer figure and garment forms, and background support planes with plausible spacing, coherent overlap, and occlusion between paper planes; cast shadows must arise from directional illumination interacting with paper thickness, cut edges, and gaps between actual-looking layers—not uniform digital drop shadows and not smooth volumetric CGI shading. Keep intentional cut negative space that clarifies arm-versus-torso separation, hair and neckline contours, gown silhouette, layered drapery openings, and overlapping fabric masses—blank background alone is insufficient, and negative cuts must remain compatible with connected or glued construction without impossible unsupported internal islands. Keep the modern fashion wardrobe modern—do not invent historical costume, jewelry, hair ornaments, inscriptions, emblems, artist signatures, museum authentication, dynasty attribution, or handmade craft provenance claims. The result must read as visually simulated layered-paper pop-up construction—not a printed photograph with a paper-texture overlay, not a flat painted illustration masquerading as cut paper, not photographic facial shading or recolored satin folds on paper shapes, not smooth plastic CGI objects, not marble or stone sculpture, not Japanese woodblock or relief-print appearance with keyblock carving or baren impression, not gongbi fine-line pigment painting, not expressive ink-wash brushwork as the primary construction, not Western watercolor, not anime or cartoon line art, and not a generic digital collage without coherent support topology. Keep a restrained full-figure 4:5 composition with shallow perspective sufficient to reveal meaningful layer spacing without changing the source stance or hiding major gown architecture.

references.notes: Authoritative private CR-001 verified import original. SHA-256 0dcf8af6cac15441d5e728f98ac53314442984d3a27a5dd193effa2bac46f41e. Outfit role preserves recognizable gown silhouette, draped neckline, and major gathered-fabric architecture for paper-layer reinterpretation—it does not lock photographic satin reflectance, every seam, every minor fold, or pixel-level dress texture; selective omission of nonessential detail into supported paper shapes is authorized.
